rationale: This is a mechanical bolt-together of two already-tested archive components (the gen-7 maintenance-adjusted flow and the gen-6 negative-oancf discontinuity) with no new economic content, and since both were evaluated on the same 0.078-coverage sample with near-identical alphas, the combination is far more likely to reshuffle the same firms than to reveal an independent effect.

A straight swap of one archived credibility weight (act/lct, gen 7) onto another archived flow definition (dp-adjusted, gen 7) is a cosmetic recombination, and the stated coverage rationale is wrong — the flow still requires sstk/prstkc/dltis/dltr, so the sample will remain bound near 0.078 rather than inheriting the liquidity variant's 0.103.

Replacing oancf/at with (oancf−dp)/at inside the credibility rank is a near-collinear reparameterization of the gen-1 baseline kink — dp/at is a slow-moving industry characteristic, so the cross-sectional rank will shift only modestly — making this too trivial a perturbation to justify a test slot.

This is a plumbing patch rather than an economic hypothesis, and it is internally compromised: dp already enters the flow term, so the ib+dp fallback weight shares a component with the signal it is meant to condition, inducing mechanical correlation in exactly the firm-years the fallback is supposed to add.

The within-firm normalization is the most genuinely novel idea in this batch and the RMW/CMA-spanning diagnosis is sound, but the expression is internally inconsistent — the short leg uses NEG(TS_RANK(·)), which is negative-valued, so after the outer SUB capital raisers receive a *positive* score that increases with their own-history cash flow, exactly reversing the stated hypothesis (the archive's working form uses a rank of the negated quality, not the negation of the rank).

This is a legitimate specification correction rather than a cosmetic variant — basing both indicators on the current-year flow restores a clean, exhaustive partition so the horizon asymmetry is actually identified — though novelty is modest and the reviewer should note that firms currently returning capital with a positive three-year average flow will contribute negatively to the long leg, so the leg is not monotone in payout.
